hook: SCP-049 talks: politely, eloquently, and with complete conviction that it is helping. Expect a character study more than a creature feature. One question is worth carrying through the whole article: what does it actually believe it is curing?
whyItMatters:
The current page opens with an author's note explaining that it is a collaboration with djkaktus, written to bring an older version of the plague doctor up to today's standards, with separate thanks to the people who voiced its audio logs. That makes it a clear example of how the wiki revisits its classics: the core image stays, while interviews, recorded audio and a full arc are layered on top.

The plague-doctor silhouette is instantly recognizable, and the rewrite gives that familiar figure an inner life to match. It is a good entry point for readers who want an SCP that works as a character piece rather than a pure monster file.
thingsToNotice:
The article moves from a cordial first interview through fussy, almost likable observation logs to a killing that changes everything. The logs are graphic once you look past the polite tone: a D-class is killed with a single touch to the throat and rebuilt with a hand pump and copper tubing into something with extra manufactured limbs that moans through a slot in its sternum, and a cow is jolted back to its feet with its head turned upside down and its legs rearranged.

The footnotes quietly answer what the main text leaves open: the robes are a grown hide, the mask is chitin rooted in its facial bones, it claims to come from 15th-century France, and its precious journals are in no known language and have never been decoded, and the attending researcher's note that 049 may know its results never change then reframes everything after it.

On 16 April 2017, 049 asks Dr. Hamm whether he feels well, kills him when he insists on the interview, and spends the next three hours turning him into an SCP-049-2 before anyone finds the body. The interview that follows is the emotional peak, with 049's justifications fraying into broken repetition until it declares that it is the cure itself. A few weeks later it is composed again, has concluded that only living patients will do, and answers the news that it will be refused with a laugh.
